title:
Every time the EC rule changed,
*prices followed*

lines.say: Your household earns 17,000 dollars a month. Until now, a new EC was out of reach. Soon, it isn't.
lines.cap: you earn *$17,000 a month*. soon, a new EC is in reach

lines.say: In August, the EC income ceiling went up from 16,000 to 18,000 dollars, for EC sites sold from now on.
lines.cap: the EC income ceiling rose to *$18,000*
lines.stat: For EC sites sold from Aug 2026

lines.say: It's not the first time. It was 10,000 dollars until 2011. Then 12,000. Then 14,000 in 2015. Then 16,000 in 2019.
Each change let more families in. And EC prices kept climbing.
In 2015, new ECs sold at about 800 dollars per square foot. By 2025, about 1,750 dollars.
A higher ceiling doesn't set prices on its own. But more eligible buyers usually means more demand for the same few launches.
If you've just become eligible, compare the new EC with resale ECs and condos nearby before you choose.
lines.cap: compare with *resale ECs and condos nearby*

lines.say: Just became eligible for an EC? Comment eligible, and we'll show you what fits your budget.

caption:
The EC income ceiling just rose to $18,000. It's not the first time. 📈

$10,000 until 2011, then $12,000, $14,000 in 2015, $16,000 in 2019. Each change let more families in, and new EC prices went from about $800 psf in 2015 to about $1,750 psf in 2025. A higher ceiling doesn't set prices on its own, but more eligible buyers usually means more demand.

Just became eligible? Comment ELIGIBLE and we'll show you what fits your budget 👇

Past trends don't guarantee future prices.
